newsitem.title: USA: Salomon says Berkshire to convert preferreds.
newsitem.headline: Salomon says Berkshire to convert preferreds.

text.p: Salomon Inc said on Thursday Berkshire Hathaway had filed a Schedule 13D and would soon convert its 1996 tranche of 140,000 Salomon preferred shares.

Berkshire also said in the 13D it might sell notes exchangeable for Salomon Inc common stock at a premium above the stock's market price at the time the notes were issued, Salomon said in a statement.
Berkshire would remain a large company shareholder and that Berkshire investor Warren Buffett and Vice President Charles Munger would remain on the Salomon Board of Directors, Salomon said.

"We are pleased to receive early advice of Berkshire Hathaway's expectation that it will convert the 1996 tranche of convertible preferred stock," Salomon Chief Executive Officer Robert Denham said in a statement. "We look forward to Berkshire remaining a large shareholder and to continuation of the contributions of Warren Buffett and Charles Munger on our Board."
